text.p: German carmaker Mercedes-Benz AG on Monday broke down its sales and profit figures for the U.S. and said group turnover increased to over 12 billion marks in 1996, up from 11.8 billion marks a year previously.

The U.S. unit saw higher profit in 1996 compared the previous year, while revenue from the car sector grew to six billion marks from 5.5 billion marks, Juergen Hubbert, board member responsible for cars, said in Detroit on Monday,
Mercedes-Benz sold 90,844 cars in the U.S., up from 76,752 units, which represents a hike of 18.4 percent and is the second-best result in the history of Mercedes USA.
The group, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG, is forecasting sales of over 100,000 vehicles in 1997.
Mercedes had already reported that total 1996 sales were 77 billion marks, up from 72.03 billion marks the year before.
